items.title: How 3D maps might help save forests
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>Scientists have created the largest collection of 3D forest maps, using laser data to reveal tree height and structure across 56 countries. The Global Canopy Atlas, led by University of Bristol researchers, could help scientists better understand carbon storage, biodiversity and how forests respond to climate change, supporting conservation and restoration efforts. (Produced by Mustakim Hasnath.)

items.title: Heavy rain winds down in New Jersey and Delaware after storms
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>Heavy rain over the East Coast is winding down, with power slowly being restored to hundreds of thousands of customers. The storms led to travel disruptions, downed trees and water rescues from New York to Virginia. Wet snow was falling as far south as the Tennessee Valley, while freezing rain moved across northern New England. (AP video shot by Tassanee Vejpongsa, Mingson Lau)

items.title: Ukrainian children return from Russia in an operation mediated by Melania Trump
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>Ukrainian children returned from Russian-occupied territories and Russia, reunited with their mothers and relatives at the northern border on Friday after years of separation, in an operation mediated by US first lady Melania Trump. Nine children and a 29-year-old former resident of a specialised boarding school were brought back to Ukraine. (AP Video shot Vasilisa Stepanenko)

items.title: Spain’s economy is thriving. Why aren’t voters feeling it?
items.author: Associated Press
items.content:
<article>Spain’s economy has been growing faster than most of its European peers, but many Spaniards haven’t felt the benefits. Discontent, particularly around soaring housing costs, is widespread and bound to be a decisive force in Sunday’s national election.

items.title: He used to be on the streets. Now he wows crowds with his homemade DJ decks
items.author: Associated Press
items.content: <article>Paul Mwangi, or 'Deejay Boboss,' became a sought-after entertainer through a journey that has been anything but ordinary. From struggling through school to living on the streets of Nairobi, he found a lifeline in music, using his self-taught electronic skills to build a wooden DJ deck.</article>
